title: One far wall is invisible at even sides
claim: Obstructed under the frozen criterion: B1 (at every even side either half-strip's corner series is the quadrant's C(w^4)) and B2 (at odd sides they differ first at 4n) are not proved; by RETURN-LAW-20261110-001A's Theorem 3, B1 at n is the identity (*1D) on the path of n - 1 vertices. Proved (refereed): Proposition 6, (a) the two half-strips have the same corner series, (b) the four-periodic vector (t, t + 1/t, 1/t, 0, ...) is an eigenvector of the strip [0, N] x Z with eigenvalue t + 1/t exactly at even sides, (c) the two-site transfer matrix squares to I on that branch. Computed: B1 at every even side 2 to 64 below w^2400 (to 80 below w^3200 in the stress test), B2 at every odd side 3 to 63 (to 79); without the bottom wall the far wall is seen first at 4n at every side 2 to 40.
failure_conditions: An even side at which a half-strip's corner return series is not C(w^4) (computed false below w^1200 at 2 to 38).
An odd side at which the half-strip and the quadrant agree before time 4n or at 4n (computed false at 3 to 21).
remaining_obligations: (*1D) on the paths with an odd number of vertices
foundation_claim_scope: The square torus of rule-60 rings with equally spaced law-(12, 12) contacts, cut open by a ring of cuts each way (A30, A32, A37, A38), its walk over GF(2), and the same walk with one or both far walls removed. Returns are a contact-level reading, so they do not depend on how the rings are declared beyond which contacts each ring holds (A45).
